reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) confirms that adding Ni or Co to Al0.8NbTiV forms sigma precipitates and improves yield strength up to 700 °C, but it does not mention or support the need for a controlled aging treatment (850–1150 °C) to induce these precipitates; the evidence shows the effect in as-cast condition.
premises: Adding ~0.2 at.% Ni or Co to Al0.8NbTiV forms homogeneously distributed sigma precipitates
These sigma precipitates improve yield strength at elevated temperatures
The baseline Al0.8NbTiV is a single-phase BCC alloy with good strength-ductility balance
A controlled aging treatment (850–1150 °C) is required to induce the sigma precipitates
The strengthening mechanism is precipitation hardening via dislocation-precipitate interactions
